- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for 1–3 days ahead.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.0), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–3% for 1–3 days ahead.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no sentiment signal, it often overestimates; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average.
- If model shows steady downward trend with no sentiment signal, it often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates > 5% from model, check sentiment history: if sentiment was neutral or negative, model likely missed downward trend; if positive, missed upward momentum.
- If sentiment history shows repeated small positive signals (0.00–0.20), model often fails to capture mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% downward correction after 3–5 days of upward trend.
